text:
alex: Heads up — seeing sustained NVMe write latency and IOPS saturation on the p3 fleet in us-west-2. Multiple pods hit OOM/eviction due to local disk pressure. dmesg has repeated 'blk_update_request: critical target error'. :eyes:

chris: Any recent kernel or driver updates in that region? can you share iostat and df -h? are these ephemeral instance NVMe or attached drives?

alex: ephemeral NVMe (instance-local). quick snaps from affected node: 
```
$ iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s  r/s  w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1: 0.00  0.00 10.00 950.00  512.00  98304.00 206.00  12.3 15.8   0.5    16.0   0.90  95.0
```
and df shows /var/lib/pods on nvme0n1 with 84% usage.

meera: That avgqu-sz and %util look brutal — sounds like IOPS saturation + long queue. Check SMART/TEMPeratures and whether wear_leveling is high. Also can try `fstrim -v /` and reduce io_scheduler or mount with `nofail` mounting? If wear is high, devices may present intermittent errors causing corruption.

maria: Also noticed ephemeral-cleaner timer failing on a few nodes in us-west-2 earlier today: 
```
Apr 4 08:12:03 node-123 systemd[1]: Started ephemeral-cleaner.timer.
Apr 4 08:12:05 ephemeral-cleaner[8723]: rm: cannot remove '/mnt/ephemeral/oldtmp/obj123': Input/output error
Apr 4 08:12:05 ephemeral-cleaner[8723]: exiting with code 1
```

alex: exact error when trying to purge tmp: `rm: Input/output error` — implies underlying device error/corruption. We also saw one pod with read errors on checkpoint files.

sre-bot: storage-alert: NVMe error rate exceeded threshold on asg-p3-usw2-2 (5xx I/O errors in 10m). Auto-eviction policy applied to top-3 noisy pods.

chris: Mitigation plan: 1) cordon + drain the most-affected nodes, 2) run offline diagnostics (smartctl, badblocks) on evacuated nodes, 3) replace failing instances (warranty/RMA) or move to instances with attached EBS if urgent. Also consider temporary scaling of dedicated capacity to avoid customer impact. Feels like a mix of hardware wear + high write patterns (checkpointing + big batches).

meera: Agreed. For short term we can also tune kernel `block` parameters and throttle writeback (vm.dirty_*), and enable prefix/KV cache to reduce disk writes from model checkpoints. Run fio to validate sustained IOPS after draining.

alex: Can someone own cordon/drain and RMA coordination? I'll keep monitoring.

maria: I'll take ownership. Starting cordon+drain of 3 nodes now (`kubectl cordon node-123 && kubectl drain node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`). Posting progress. :thumbsup:

chris: If you hit nodes with persistent corruption, mark them for return and avoid reusing the same NVMe class for heavy checkpoint workloads until we adjust scheduling policies. Could add a taint `storage=faulty:NoSchedule` to prevent reuse.

meera: After drains complete, I'll run fio 4k/randrw for 10m to confirm IOPS and run `smartctl -a` to capture wear indicators. If SMART shows critical attributes (Media_Wearout, Reallocated_Sector_Ct) we proceed with RMA.

alex: Thanks — I'll also add a short-term routing policy to steer heavy checkpoint jobs to EBS-backed instances and reduce batch sizes for training jobs in us-west-2. Will update once metrics stabilize.

maria: 1/3 drained, starting diagnostics on node-123. Will post logs here.

chris: Thanks team — keep notes for postmortem. We may need quota/cost discussion if we shift to EBS temporarily (higher unit cost) vs replacing NVMe hardware.

alex: noted for cost. creating a minimal postmortem draft after we have final RMA and capacity numbers.

maria: update: smartctl shows increased Media_Wearout and 2 reallocated sectors on node-123. tagging node for replacement.

meera: good call. I'll schedule RMA and run full badblocks overnight on the evacuated instance images.

alex: solid. thanks everyone.
